name: Automatic Layout Generation
description: Machine learning-based lithography hotspot detection has been deeply studied recently, from varies feature extraction techniques to efficient learning models. It has been observed that such machine learning-based frameworks are providing satisfactory metal layer hotspot prediction results on known public metal layer benchmarks. In this work, we seek to evaluate how these machine learning-based hotspot detectors generalize to complicated patterns. We first introduce a automatic layout generation tool that can synthesize varies layout patterns given a set of design rules. The tool currently supports both metal layer and via layer generation. As a case study, we conduct hotspot detection on the generated via layer layouts with representative machine learning-based hotspot detectors, which shows that continuous study on model robustness and generality is necessary to prototype and integrate the learning engines in DFM flows. evaluation_method: accuracy / detection performance on generated layouts
reputation: A niche benchmark/tooling paper in lithography hotspot detection, mainly used to test robustness and generalization of ML-based DFM models.
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark; primarily a synthetic layout generation setup for robustness testing, so results depend on the generated rule set and hotspot definition.
